title: Bearings
keyIdea: A bearing gives a direction as an angle measured from North, turning clockwise, written with three figures: East is 090°, South 180°, West 270°, and 5° is written 005°. To measure the bearing of B from A, stand at A, face North and turn clockwise until you face B. The bearing back again, of A from B, differs by exactly 180°, because the North lines at A and B are parallel: add 180° if the bearing is under 180°, otherwise take 180° away. Bearings and a scale drawing together let you plot a route and find how far and in what direction the finish is from the start.
familyTip: On a walk or a map app, pick a landmark and stand facing North (most phones have a compass). Estimate the bearing of the landmark, then check it. Ask: what is the bearing back home from the landmark? It should be 180° different.

visual.caption: A correctly written bearing, or not? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: swing an arm from North to set and measure bearings, point back from B to A, pick back bearings, and read a trip's bearing.

kid: A bearing tells you a direction as an angle. There are three rules. Start facing North. Turn clockwise. Write the angle with three figures.
So East is 090°, South is 180° and West is 270°. An angle of 5° is written 005°. North-west is halfway between West and North, so it is 315°.
To find the bearing of B from A, stand at A. Face North. Turn clockwise until you face B. The angle you turned is the bearing.
The way back is different. If B is on 070° from A, then A is on 250° from B. Add 180°. If the bearing is 180° or more, take 180° away instead. That keeps it under 360°.
adult: Ages 13 to 15. In England, bearings appear in Key Stage 3 geometry and measures (measure angles, interpret maps and scale drawings, and use bearings) and again in GCSE content G15. Learners need the angle facts for parallel lines, accurate use of a protractor, and scale drawing. Bearings feed into later work with vectors, trigonometry in navigation, and the sine and cosine rules.

The three conventions are: measure from North, measure clockwise, and give three figures, so values run from 000° to 359°. A back bearing differs by 180° because the North lines through the two points are parallel; the angles where line AB crosses them are co-interior, so they add to 180°. On a trip of 4 km on 090° then 3 km on 180°, the finish is 5 km from the start on a bearing of about 127°, because tan of the extra angle is 3 ÷ 4.

Accurate drawing matters. Draw a North line at every point you measure from, put the protractor's centre on that point, and line up its zero with North. Estimate first: a bearing pointing into the south-west must be between 180° and 270°.

Common mistakes: measuring anticlockwise (reading 050° for a north-west point that is really 310°), measuring from East or from the line of travel, writing 45° instead of 045°, giving the same bearing for the return trip, using 180° minus the bearing or 360° minus the bearing for a back bearing, and ending up with values over 360°. The lab tests each of these: you set and measure bearings with a draggable arm, point back from B, choose back bearings and read a trip's bearing from a scale drawing.

practice.prompt: What is the bearing of due South?
practice.hint: Start at North and turn clockwise. South is half a full turn.
practice.explain: South is half a turn clockwise from North, so 180°. 090° is East and 270° is West.

practice.prompt: B is on a bearing of {b}° from A. What is the bearing of A from B, in degrees?
practice.hint: The back bearing differs by 180°. Is the bearing under 180°?
practice.explain: {b} is under 180, so add 180: the bearing of A from B is {=b+180}°.

practice.prompt: A lighthouse is on a bearing of {b}° from a boat. What is the bearing of the boat from the lighthouse, in degrees?
practice.hint: The bearing is 180° or more, so take 180° away.
practice.explain: {b} − 180 = {=b-180}, so the boat is on a bearing of {=b-180}° from the lighthouse (written with three figures).

practice.prompt: Kai writes a bearing of 8° as 8°. How should it be written?
practice.hint: Bearings always have three figures. Where do the zeros go?
practice.explain: Put zeros in front to make three figures: 008°. 080° is a different direction, 80°, and 800° is not a bearing.

practice.prompt: A plane flies north-east. What is its bearing?
practice.hint: North-east is halfway between North (000°) and East (090°).
practice.explain: Halfway between 000° and 090° is 045°. 315° is north-west and 135° is south-east.

pool.prompt: Which direction is a bearing of 270°?
pool.hint: Turn clockwise from North: East is 090°, South 180°.
pool.explain: Three quarter turns clockwise from North face West, so 270° is West. East would be 090°.

pool.prompt: B is on a bearing of 120° from A. What is the bearing of A from B?
pool.explain: 120 + 180 = 300, so A is on 300° from B. 060° is 180 − 120, and 120° is the bearing of B from A, not the way back.

pool.prompt: Mo measures from North but turns anticlockwise, and gets 040°. What is the real bearing?
pool.hint: An anticlockwise turn of 40° is the same as a clockwise turn of 360° − 40°.
pool.explain: Turning 40° anticlockwise ends where a 320° clockwise turn ends, so the bearing is 320°.

pool.prompt: A boat sails 4 km on 090°, then 3 km on 180°. How far is it from the start?
pool.hint: The legs make a right angle. Use Pythagoras.
pool.explain: The legs meet at a right angle, so the distance is √(4² + 3²) = √25 = 5 km. 7 km is the distance sailed, not the straight-line distance.

pool.prompt: A ship is on a bearing of {b}° from a port. What is the bearing of the port from the ship, in degrees?
pool.hint: The bearing is over 180°, so take 180° away.
pool.explain: {b} − 180 = {=b-180}. The port is on a bearing of {=b-180}° from the ship.

pool.prompt: Why does a back bearing differ by exactly 180°?
choices: The North lines at A and B are parallel, so co-interior angles with AB add to 180°
pool.hint: Draw North lines at both points. How are they related?
pool.explain: North lines at A and B are parallel. The line AB crosses both, making co-interior angles that add to 180°, so the bearings differ by 180°.

pool.hint: Count the figures. A bearing always has three.
pool.explain: 062° has three figures. 62° is missing the leading zero, and a bearing needs no compass letter.

pool.prompt: Ella says the bearing of A from B is 360° minus the bearing of B from A. Test her rule with 070°.
choices: Wrong: 360 − 70 = 290°, but the back bearing is 250°
pool.explain: The back bearing of 070° is 070 + 180 = 250°. Her rule gives 290°, which flips East and West instead of turning round.

pool.prompt: A buoy is on a bearing of {b}° from a ship. What is the bearing of the ship from the buoy, in degrees?
pool.hint: The bearing is under 180°, so add 180°.
pool.explain: {b} + 180 = {=b+180}, so the ship is on a bearing of {=b+180}° from the buoy.

pool.prompt: A boat sails 4 km due East, then 3 km due South. Which bearing takes it straight back to the start?
pool.hint: The bearing of the finish from the start is about 127°. Going back is a back bearing.
pool.explain: The finish is on about 127° from the start, so the start is on 127 + 180 ≈ 307° from the finish. 127° is the outward bearing.
